const GUARD_NULL_STORE_MESSAGE: string = "This stores `null` through a guard into a slot that holds an object, and a guard stores only a number, a `boolean`, an enum or a `string`, and a `null` only into a `string | null` slot, where the store frees the copy the slot held; keep a `boolean` field beside the slot, `g.value.hasNext = false`, and test it before reading the object"
const TASK_WRITE_TAIL: string = ", and `spawn` runs it beside the scope's other tasks: make scratch only this task uses inside it, because an object handed in as the argument is shared memory even when the `spawn` made it, since where an argument was made is not tracked. Write memory the tasks share only through the guard of a `Mutex`; "
const TASK_WRITE_ADVICE: string = "hand a value the parent needs back as the task's answer"
const CHANNEL_DECLARE_TAIL: string = ": a channel is a `const` declared in the block that holds its scope's `using s = scope()`, or in the block that has the scope's block as one of its statements, before it, so each run of the declaration makes a channel for one run of one scope"
const CHANNEL_USE_TAIL: string = ": a channel is used only as the receiver of `send`, the iterable of a `for...of`, an argument, or a field its class's constructor sets from a parameter, so it is never bound, stored, returned or captured, and which tasks reach it is a question the checker can answer; hand it to the task as its argument, `s.spawn(task, ch)`, or as a field the argument's constructor sets, `s.spawn(task, new Work(ch, n))`"
const CHANNEL_SENDERS_TAIL: string = ": a channel is reachable from the tasks of one scope, the parent sends on it only before the block that holds that scope's spawns, and nobody closes it: it closes once the scope has started to join and every task that may send on it has returned"
const CHANNEL_RECEIVER_TAIL: string = ": a channel has one receiver, either one task spawned outside any loop or the parent in a later statement of the block that has the scope's block as one of its statements, and inside a scope's block the parent receives nothing, so the parent's one wait is the join; receive in one task spawned outside the loop, or after the scope's block, `{ using s = scope(); ... } for (const x of ch) { ... }`"
const CHANNEL_ORDER_TAIL: string = ": under Node a task runs where it is spawned, so every task that may send on a channel is spawned, in the block's statement order, before the one task that receives on it, which is also what keeps channels from deadlocking; move the `spawn` of the receiving task below every `spawn` that sends"
const CHANNEL_BOTH_TAIL: string = ": no task both sends and receives on one channel, because a channel closes only once every task that may send on it has returned, and this one would wait in its own loop for its own return; split it into a task that sends and a task that receives, or answer the result through a second channel"
